docs/GLOSSARY.md:13:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an **engine-presented gate** appears when a backward edge's bound is spent: after `max_iterations` traversals, or immediately on the first failure where that bound is **zero**, which is how a step whose verdict is a refusal reaches a human without spending a round first (Q-0083). It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`. It is called an *exhaustion* gate only where a loop actually ran; at a bound of zero nothing looped, and the engine says so rather than reporting a loop that did not happen.
docs/GLOSSARY.md:69:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

docs/decisions/011-bounded-backward-edges-in-the-flow-engine.md:2:**Decision:** Steps and routes may declare `on_fail: goto <step | flow:name>` with a mandatory `max_iterations`, a named counter persisted in the ticket, and `on_exhausted: gate`. Cross-flow backward edges (review → development, qa-final → development/solutioning) are allowed. Exhausted loops and exceeded budgets always land on a human gate.
docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:2:**Decision:** Answering `retry` at an exhaustion gate sets **that loop's** counter to `max_iterations`, so the retry's own `goto` is the single authorised traversal and the next failure re-presents the gate. No other counter is touched, and the grant is recorded in `runs.log` as `gate=retry counter=<name> set=<n>`. For the shipped review flow (`max_iterations: 3`) a retry persists `3`; the traversal it triggers is the fourth and last, and a further rejection lands back on the gate.
docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:3:**Alternatives considered:** (a) Persist `max_iterations - 1`, proposed by the Q-0006 round-2 review — off by one: the retry's own regression is a traversal, so the following rejection increments to `max_iterations` and regresses *again*, granting two. (b) The behaviour actually shipped, `ctx.counters = {}` — worse in two ways: it granted `max_iterations + 1` further traversals, and it wiped every counter on the ticket, so a review retry silently refunded a `qa` budget the ticket had already spent. (c) A separate `grace` field in the flow file — more explicit, but a second number to keep consistent with `max_iterations` and nothing yet needs the two to differ.
docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:4:**Why:** AC-18 of Q-0006's requirement says retry "authorises exactly one more traversal", and three sources disagreed about what that meant: the requirement, `contracts/Q-0006/review-runtime.contract.md`, and the scenarios QA wrote. The engine settled it — traced against `handleFail` and `runGate`, only `max_iterations` yields exactly one. The Q-0006 reviewer caught this in round 4 and, notably, corrected its own round-2 recommendation to get there.
docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:6:**Contract erratum, not a silent override.** `review-runtime.contract.md` says `max_iterations - 1`, and the contracts are frozen — every task in `tasks.yaml` forbids editing `contracts/Q-0006/**`. Letting QA's test assert `max_iterations` against a contract saying otherwise would mean a test quietly outvoting a contract, which is exactly the failure the frozen-contract rule exists to prevent. The amendment is therefore explicit: `backlog/Q-0006-…/solution/errata.md`, dated, naming the superseded clause, referenced from the ticket. Development implements the erratum; the contract file itself is corrected by whichever ticket next opens it legitimately.

    80	**Two shapes appear above, and the difference is which run reads the file.** An artifact its own
    81	flow reads is named by the run that wrote it — and by the iteration too, where a bounded loop can
    82	rewrite it — so nothing a run produces is destroyed by the next round or the next run. An artifact a
    83	**later** flow reads cannot be, because `{run}` interpolates to the *reading* run's id and a
    84	consumer two runs later would glob an empty directory; those four are written twice, as a per-run
    85	copy for history and a flat **pointer** at the stable name the consumer knows. `review/verdict.md`
     1	// `ticket.md` frontmatter — the ten fields the backlog writes, as they are written.
     2	//
     3	// What is required and what is optional follows one rule: THE SCHEMA REQUIRES WHAT
     4	// `Backlog.create()` ALWAYS WRITES (spike/src/backlog.js:60-68), EXCEPT WHERE A READER SUPPLIES
     5	// ITS OWN FALLBACK. So `iterations` and `history` are optional, because the engine reads them as
     6	// `?? {}` and `?? []` (spike/src/engine.js:44, :634, :661, :745) and a ticket without them is a
     7	// ticket the engine already runs; everything else is required, because the only writer writes it
     8	// unconditionally and every one of the 27 tickets in this repository carries it.
     9	//
    10	// Nothing here carries a default. `parseFrontmatter` itself requires no field and invents none
    11	// (spike/src/backlog.js:11-15); a zod default would hand thirteen later tickets a value the file
    12	// did not contain, and no test would fail.

    17	/**
    18	 * One entry in a ticket's run history. `outcome()` (spike/src/engine.js:655-657) writes EIGHT
    19	 * fields, and docs/02-sdlc-pipeline-spec.md showed four until this change corrected it.
    20	 *
    21	 * The three that are optional are optional because SHORTER ENTRIES EXIST ON DISK: five of the 59
    22	 * entries in this repository predate `status`, `stage_before` and `stage_after`. Rejecting them
    23	 * would be a migration, not a port — and `contracts/Q-0006/ticket-review-state.schema.json`
    24	 * already models the older shape as a separate branch of its own union.
    25	 *
    26	 * `stage` duplicates `stage_after` in every entry the current writer produces. That is a known
    27	 * redundancy, reported rather than fixed: the port preserves behaviour.
    28	 */
    29	export const ticketHistoryEntrySchema = z.looseObject({
    30	  stage: stageSchema,
    31	  /** The run number, allocated from `runs.log` — spike/src/engine.js:744-751. */
    32	  run: z.number(),
    33	  /** The flow's `name`, not a stage. Hand-written entries name one-off flows too. */
    34	  flow: z.string(),
    35	  /** completed | regressed | aborted | failed | interrupted | undecided | exhausted. Typed open: the
    36	   * run status vocabulary belongs to whichever package needs it twice (spike/bin/harness.js:131),
    37	   * and Q-0049 and Q-0050 own that decision. `undecided` is Q-0040's: a run that reached a gate no
    38	   * answer was available for, which moves no stage. */
    39	  status: z.string().optional(),
    40	  stage_before: stageSchema.optional(),
    41	  stage_after: stageSchema.optional(),
    42	  /** An ISO 8601 instant, as `new Date().toISOString()` writes it. */
    43	  at: z.string(),
    44	  /**
    45	   * Billed cost in USD, or null. Null is "the vendor reported no price", which is not zero — it is
    46	   * rendered `n/a` beside a token count and never `$0.000` ("Codex cost is reported as tokens,
    47	   * never priced locally", docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-22).
    48	   */
    49	  cost: z.number().nullable(),
    50	});

    52	export const ticketSchema = z.looseObject({
    53	  id: z.string(),
    54	  title: z.string(),
    55	  /** The ticket's position in the state machine, and only that. Where the code IS is derived from
    56	   * git on every `board` invocation and stored nowhere. */
    57	  stage: stageSchema,
    58	  /**
    59	   * The human who owns the CURRENT stage, or the sentinel `unknown` where nobody said.
    60	   *
    61	   * Supplied by whichever surface created the ticket and never guessed by `core`. See *"A ticket's
    62	   * owner is supplied, never guessed"* (2026-09-08).
    63	   */
    64	  owner: z.string(),
    65	  /** Only meaningful in the central backlog layout. Written and never read. */
    66	  repos: z.array(z.string()),
    67	  /** The ticket's integration branch — `harness/<id>/integration` (spike/src/backlog.js:64). */
    68	  branch: z.string(),
    69	  /** Written and never read (spike/src/backlog.js:64). */
    70	  priority: z.string(),
    71	  /**
    72	   * A date STRING, not a date value: `create()` writes `…toISOString().slice(0, 10)`
    73	   * (spike/src/backlog.js:65) and the YAML core schema has no timestamp type, so it round-trips as
    74	   * `YYYY-MM-DD` text. The shape is not enforced, because nothing enforces it today.
    75	   */
    76	  created: z.string(),
    77	  /**
    78	   * Loop counters, by name. BOTH key forms occur on disk and both are legal:
    79	   *
    80	   *   - the dotted `<flow>.<step>` the engine computes when a step declares no counter —
   175	    // Flow.name is optional in the schema and required in a history entry; lintFlow rejects a
   176	    // flow without one, so every flow reaching a run has it. Preserved: the spike writes it raw.
   177	    stage: after as TicketHistoryEntry['stage'], run: context.runId, flow: context.flow.name as string, status,
   178	    stage_before: before as TicketHistoryEntry['stage_before'],
   179	    stage_after: after as TicketHistoryEntry['stage_after'], at: new Date().toISOString(), cost,
   180	  };
   181	}
   182	
   183	/**
   184	 * Persist a non-terminal occurrence event without moving the ticket's stage.
   185	 *
   186	 * The sole owner of this mutation. `RunPersistence.recordOccurrenceEvent` is the seam `routing.ts`
   187	 * reaches it through and delegates straight back here; implementing the same four writes on both
   188	 * sides appended two history entries and two log lines for one exhaustion.
   189	 */
   190	export async function recordEvent(context: LifecycleContext, stage: string, status: string, cost: number | null): Promise<void> {
   191	  context.ticket.meta.iterations = context.counters;
   192	  context.ticket.meta.history = [...(context.ticket.meta.history ?? []), outcome(context, stage, stage, status, cost)];
   193	  context.persistence.writeTicket(context.ticket);
   194	  context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} ${status} stage=${stage}→${stage} cost=${cost}`);
   195	  return Promise.resolve();
   196	}

   198	/**
   199	 * Narrow the optional argument at the sole status branch where the contract requires it.
   200	 *
   201	 * Why: deliberate addition, not preservation — the spike spreads `...fields` and cannot throw. A
   202	 * runtime backstop is kept because AC-3's closed union crosses a process boundary in M3, and it
   203	 * throws the workspace's `FlowError` so a consumer reads a sentence like every other engine failure.
   204	 */
   205	function requiredRegressionFields(fields: RegressionFields | undefined): RegressionFields {
   206	  if (!fields) throw new FlowError('regressed run requires complete regression fields');
   207	  return fields;
   208	}

   465	    // (`steps.ts`), so the order is the mechanism and not presentation: `blocked|proceed` would gate

   467	    for (const [name, text] of chores()) {
   468	      expect(text, `${name}: implement declares no verdict`).toContain('verdict: proceed|blocked');
   469	    }
   470	  });
   471	
   472	  test('and it is bounded at zero, so the first refusal is the gate rather than the last', () => {
   473	    // The whole ticket: with any positive bound a refusal buys a round that cannot converge, which
   474	    // Q-0091 and Q-0101 each paid for — $45.44 between them, in rounds that changed no files.
   475	    for (const [name, text] of chores()) {
   476	      expect(text, `${name}: implement's bound is not zero`)
   477	        .toMatch(/on_fail:\s*\{\s*goto:\s*implement,\s*max_iterations:\s*0,\s*on_exhausted:\s*gate\s*\}/);
   478	    }
   479	  });
   480	
   481	  test('and a retry round reads its own previous report, which is what makes the edge converge', () => {
   482	    // Required by the convergence rule — a backward edge must send the target something it reads —
   483	    // and right on its own: the round after an erratum should see what it refused last time.
   484	    for (const [name, text] of chores()) {
   485	      expect(text, `${name}: implement cannot read its own prior rounds`)
   486	        .toContain('"dev/chore/run-{run}/implement-iter-*.md"');
   487	    }
   488	  });
   489	
   490	  test('the role that answers it knows what blocked means, and what it does not', () => {
   491	    // A verdict no agent understands is a field nobody sets. The line that matters is the negative
   492	    // one: `blocked` is an authority appeal and not a difficulty report, and no lint can tell them
   493	    // apart — which is why the ticket routed it to a human gate rather than to a validator.
   494	    for (const role of ['harness/roles/developer-generalist.md',
   495	                        'packages/cli/templates/harness/roles/developer-generalist.md']) {
   496	      const text = repoFile(role);
   497	      expect(text, `${role}: the role never mentions the verdict it must return`).toContain('blocked');
   498	      expect(text, `${role}: the role does not say what blocked is NOT for`)
   499	        .toMatch(/not for work that is large, unclear or hard/);
   500	    }
   501	  });
   502	});

    23	/**
    24	 * The eight values the schema's run-level `status` enum admits.
    25	 *
    26	 * Seven of them are terminal and one is not, which is the only distinction any caller draws.
    27	 * `exhausted` is legal and the engine never writes it: exhaustion is recorded as a ticket-history
    28	 * event and the run continues to a gate, ending later with its actual outcome. That is a note about
    29	 * the caller and not a restriction here — the writer's `finalise` writes whichever it is given.
    30	 *
    31	 * One union serves both levels, and since Q-0040 the two levels no longer admit the same set:
    32	 * `undecided` is a run's conclusion about itself and never a step's, because a gate allocates no
    33	 * occurrence and nothing one level down can be undecided. What refuses it there is the schema's
    34	 * separate occurrence enum and the guard over it, not this type.
    35	 */
    36	export type RunStatus = 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'aborted' | 'regressed' | 'exhausted' | 'interrupted' | 'undecided';
    37	
    38	/**
    39	 * What an occurrence was: an adapter call, a script step, or an integrate step.
    40	 *
    41	 * Nothing else allocates one. A gate and a fan-out parent schedule work rather than perform it, so
    42	 * neither appears in `steps` at all.
    43	 */
    48	
    49	  constructor(message: string, gate: UnansweredGate) {
    50	    super(message);
    51	    this.gate = gate;
    52	  }
    53	}
    54	
    55	/**
    56	 * A run's six closed terminal statuses. `exhausted` is not among them — it is a history-only
    57	 * status a bounded loop records at its own limit, before the gate it then asks decides whether the
    58	 * run continues; see {@link RunPersistence.recordOccurrenceEvent}.
    59	 *
    60	 * `undecided` is a *run* status and never an occurrence status or a gate answer: it says the run
    61	 * reached a gate no answer was available for, so nothing was decided. See Q-0040.
    62	 */
    63	export type RunStatus = 'completed' | 'regressed' | 'aborted' | 'failed' | 'interrupted' | 'undecided';
